record.what_it_does: Website builder and ecommerce platform; Commerce APIs expose products, orders, inventory, contacts, and more.
record.auth_notes: API keys (site owner generates them in Settings > Advanced > Developer API Keys) are for custom apps on a single site. OAuth is for commercial multi-site apps, and the Webhook Subscriptions API is OAuth only.
record.access_notes: An API key needs the Commerce Advanced plan, a paid plan. OAuth clients must be reviewed and approved on the Squarespace developer apps page before other sites can connect. Approval only allows OAuth connections. Listing in Squarespace Extensions is a separate process. I did not verify whether a dev-mode OAuth client works on your own site before approval.
record.api_breadth_notes: About 9 APIs: Analytics, Contacts, Discounts, Inventory, Orders, Products, Profiles (maintenance mode), Transactions, Webhook Subscriptions, plus Websites and Forms (read-only). I did not count individual operations.
record.mcp_notes: A search found no official Squarespace MCP server. Third-party ones exist: community servers on GitHub, and hosted ones from Zapier, StackOne, MCPBundles and others.
record.blocker_notes: The OAuth client needs Squarespace approval before public use. Testing without OAuth approval needs a Commerce Advanced site for an API key. The API covers commerce only, not site content or design. Whether the page-builder surface is reachable is unclear.

evidence.quote: API keys will never expire as long as the merchant site remains active.
Custom applications require Squarespace's Commerce Advanced plan.
Webhook Subscriptions: Subscribes to site notifications, such as when an order is created

record.needs_human: Confirm whether a dev-mode OAuth client works before approval. Confirm whether an OpenAPI spec is published and whether a sandbox exists. Neither appeared in the pages I fetched. The quotes are paraphrased summaries from the fetch tool, not verbatim page text, and the MCP quote is only a search-result title.
